subject: Performance SLOs & regional routing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, Jun 2, 2026 at 15:10 PDT
Subject: Performance SLOs & regional routing follow-up

Hi Mike / Elena —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC: 

Recap of requirements (as we understand them):
- Latency targets:
  - US: p95 < 150 ms for single-turn generation (short prompts)
  - EU: p95 < 200 ms (regional routing to EU preferred)
  - APAC: p95 < 250 ms (acceptable for initial rollout; we can iterate)
- Throughput / concurrency:
  - Sustained throughput: ~50 requests/sec (average across peak windows)
  - Burst capacity: up to ~200 requests/sec for short spikes
  - Concurrent sessions/streams: target ~500 concurrent user sessions for the first phase
- Streaming: support for chunked streaming/resume for long outputs and partial responses; clients will expect early token responses for perceived latency
- State & KV caching: will want prefix/response caching for repeated prompts; KV cache consistency across regional routing is important for continuity
- Data residency / compliance: EU customer data (payloads and logs) MUST remain in EU jurisdiction; APAC data preferred to stay in APAC where feasible
- Availability & SLOs: Finova mentioned a 99.9% uptime expectation for production endpoints

Attachments: I attached SLO_summary_v1.pdf with the above in a table and our proposed test matrix.

Proposed next steps:
1) POC perf run: Redwood will execute a controlled run against a staging instance (we'll share synthetic load scripts).
2) Provide sample request shapes / retention expectations from your side (to size token cost/IO).
3) Tech sync for routing/residency: Rishi will join to confirm how we pin traffic and handle KV cache replication across regions.
4) Commercial: Aditya / AE to propose pricing for reserved burst / on-demand mix.

I'm happy to schedule a 30–45 min technical kick-off next week. Proposed windows: Wed 6/9 10–11am PT or Thu 6/10 8–9am PT. Let me know what works and who else should join (legal for EU residency?).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. This matches our notes; a few clarifications from the Finova side: 

- EU data residency: we need both request payloads and all logs/audit trails to be stored in EU-only storage. No backups or logging replicas outside EU without prior approval.
- APAC: initial customer subset will be Japan and Australia; for phase 1 it's acceptable if latency is slightly higher, but we need a roadmap to get p95 < 200ms in APAC within 3 months of go-live.
- SLA expectations: our procurement group is targeting 99.9% availability for the inference endpoints; we'll need a proposed SLA in the contract.
- Security artifacts: please include SOC 2 Type II summary and data flow diagrams in the next packet (we've attached our requirements worksheet).

Attached: Finova_requirements.xlsx — includes retention windows and a sample request shape (average tokens ~350, max ~2k for long-form generation).

Next steps: the team is available for a technical kick-off on Thu 6/10 8am PT (that works for Elena + infra). Procurement will follow shortly after the POC if the numbers look good.

Thanks,
Mike

Thanks Mike — quick technical notes from our side: 

- Regional routing: we can pin inference requests to region-specific endpoints (US/EU/APAC). For EU data residency we can provision dedicated storage and ensure logs/audit trails remain in EU; we'll run a short compliance checklist with our security team and loop legal.
- KV cache & state: for connection stickiness across multiple calls we recommend session affinity to the same region + prefix caching. Cross-region KV replication is possible but will add to tail latency; for Finova's consistency requirements we suggest keeping session state regional for phase 1.
- Streaming & concurrency: streaming response (token-by-token) is supported. For 500 concurrent sessions we recommend a mix of continuous batching and low-latency fast-path kernels; we'll size GPU pool based on your token distribution (your spreadsheet says avg 350 tokens).
- Perf run proposal: Redwood to run synthetic tests with the following matrix: 50 sustained req/s, bursts to 200 req/s, concurrency sweep 100 -> 500 sessions, streaming enabled. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, token throughput, and cost/kg.

Action items I can take on immediately:
- Prepare a regional routing configuration for the POC and a rough cost/throughput estimate (ETA: 2 business days).
- Coordinate with infra to set up EU-only logging for the POC.
